title: Both of These Men Are About to Die #shorts
description:
Both of these men are about to die, and neither one will feel a thing.

November 5, 2005. A refinery in Delaware City, Delaware. Two men are bolting the lid back onto a tank that has been pumped full of nitrogen, and the gas is leaking out of the open hole where they work. There is no warning sign and no barrier. Their work permit says nitrogen: not applicable.

Then someone spots a roll of duct tape five feet down inside. Going in means a permit and a delay, so they stay outside and fish for it with a wire.

Nitrogen is most of the air you are breathing. One or two breaths of it on its own and you black out, with no smell, no taste and no warning. It feels like air, so you just breathe it.

You don't have to climb inside a tank for it to kill you. And if someone goes down in one: do not go in after them. Call it in.

This is an animated reconstruction. Every fact in it comes from official reports:
- U.S. Chemical Safety Board, Case Study 2006-02-I-DE, "Confined Space Entry - Worker and Would-be Rescuer Asphyxiated"
  https://www.csb.gov/valero-delaware-city-refinery-asphyxiation-incident/
- U.S. Chemical Safety Board, Safety Bulletin 2003-10-B, "Hazards of Nitrogen Asphyxiation"
  https://www.csb.gov/hazards-of-nitrogen-asphyxiation/
- OSHA Technical Manual, Section IV, Chapter 2, "Petroleum Refining Processes"
  https://www.osha.gov/otm/section-4-safety-hazards/chapter-2

We tell these stories so no other family goes through this.
Don't die at work today.

Narration is an AI voice. The animation is a reconstruction, not footage.
